faq.a: In winter their food, insects and worms, almost disappears, and keeping a small body warm in the cold would burn energy fast. Hibernating lets a hedgehog survive the winter on stored fat.
asks: Why don't hedgehogs just eat in winter?

faq.q: How slow is a hibernating hedgehog's heart?
faq.a: An active hedgehog's heart beats about 190 times a minute. In hibernation it can drop to around 20 beats a minute, and breathing may stop for several minutes at a time.
asks: Does a hedgehog's heart slow down in winter?

faq.q: How cold does a hibernating hedgehog get?
faq.a: Its body temperature can fall from about 35 degrees Celsius to around 5, close to the temperature of its nest. Its body uses only a tiny fraction of its normal energy.
asks: Is a hibernating hedgehog cold to touch?

faq.q: Do hedgehogs wake up during hibernation?
faq.a: Yes. Every week or two they warm up for a short time, possibly to let their body systems catch up, and may even move nest. Each warm-up costs a lot of stored fat.
asks: Why do hibernating animals wake up?

faq.q: How heavy must a hedgehog be to hibernate?
faq.a: A young hedgehog needs to build up enough fat in autumn to last the winter. Wildlife groups suggest that juveniles under about 450 grams in late autumn may struggle to survive hibernation.
asks: Why do hedgehogs eat so much in autumn?
Can a small hedgehog survive winter?

facts: A hibernating hedgehog's heart rate can fall from about 190 to around 20 beats per minute.
Hibernating hedgehogs rewarm briefly every week or two, which uses a large share of their fat stores.
